+import pytest
+
+from glom import Call, Fill, Path, PathAccessError, T, glom
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('target, divisor, expected', [
+    (7, 2, 3),
+    (-7, 2, -4),
+    (7, -2, -4),
+    (7.5, 2, 3.0),
+])
+def test_numeric_floor_division(target, divisor, expected):
+    result = glom(target, T // divisor)
+    assert result == expected
+    assert type(result) is type(expected)
+
+
+def test_operand_specs_and_chaining():
+    target = {'x': 17, 'y': 3}
+    assert glom(target, T['x'] // T['y']) == 5
+    assert glom(target, (T['x'] // T['y']) + 1) == 6
+    assert glom(7, -(T // 2)) == -3
+    assert glom(7, Fill([T // 2])) == [3]
+    assert glom(7, Call(tuple, args=([T // 2],))) == (3,)
+
+
+def test_floor_division_repr():
+    assert repr(T // 2) == 'T // 2'
+    assert repr(T + (T // 2)) == 'T + (T // 2)'
+    assert repr(-(T // 2)) == '-(T // 2)'
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize('value, divisor, exc_type', [
+    (1, 0, ZeroDivisionError),
+    ('x', 2, TypeError),
+])
+def test_floor_division_access_errors(value, divisor, exc_type):
+    spec = T['value'] // divisor
+    with pytest.raises(PathAccessError) as caught:
+        glom({'value': value}, spec)
+    assert isinstance(caught.value.exc, exc_type)
+    assert caught.value.part_idx == 1
+    assert caught.value.path == Path(spec)
